correctness.rationale: In R^(2m), the n=2m unsigned edge vectors e_j+e_{j+1} have affine tangent H of dimension d=n-2, equal norms squared 2-4/n, and covariance C with eigenvalues (4/n)cos²(pi k/n) over k excluding 0 and m. Cyclic transitivity yields Mahalanobis squared distance d for every vertex. Any enclosing ellipsoid shape Q satisfies tr(Q^-1 C)+(z-c)^T Q^-1(z-c)<=1. AM-GM gives det Q>=d^d det C, equality uniquely at center c, shape dC. The sine-product identity then yields semiaxis product m((m-1)/m)^(m-1), circumball factor [2(m-1)/m]^(m-1), ratio m/2^(m-1). Steps work including m=2. The actual included standalone script passed m=2..20; finite experiments supplement but do not replace proof.

originality.rationale: Publicly described even-cycle root polytopes are known; standard D-optimal design and covariance-contact optimality are credited. The new exact claim is their intrinsic unique outer Löwner ellipsoid, complete closed Fourier semiaxis spectrum and exponentially small volume ratio m/2^(m-1) to the minimum Euclidean circumball. Full-text comparisons against same-family inradius work and distinct-family outer-ellipsoid work do not yield the statement or its implication; semantic published-finding corpus and literature queries found no dominating equivalent. value.rationale: An infinite natural family of unweighted bipartite root/lattice polytopes has its full intrinsic outer ellipsoid and exact semiaxes determined. Comparing this volume-optimal ellipsoid to its true minimum circumball reveals the sharp exponentially decreasing factor m/2^(m-1), even though all 2m vertices simultaneously touch both boundaries, and the ellipsoid aspect ratio is the exact cotangent growing linearly. This quantitative metric tradeoff is useful for graph-polytope geometric approximation and experimental design; unlike mere reuse of the classical design criterion, it computes previously unidentified natural exact invariants and their all-rank behavior.
